question: Banks are required to keep some reserves in liquid form with themselves. This is called _______.
solution:
The correct answer is__** Statutory liquidity ratio.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statutory liquidity ratio (SLR)** is a **monetary policy tool **used by the **central bank of a country** to regulate the liquidity in the banking system.
 
• It requires banks to maintain a certain percentage of their **net demand and time liabilities (NDTL)** in the form of **liquid assets **such as **cash, gold, or government securities.**
 
• The SLR is determined by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** and is currently set at **18.00% of NDTL.**
 
• Banks have to maintain this SLR on a **daily basis **and report it to the RBI every fortnight.
 
• SLR serves as a cushion against** unforeseen liquidity shocks** in the banking system.
 
• It also ensures that banks have **enough liquid assets t**o meet the demands of their depositors.
 
• Banks cannot** lend or invest **the funds that are kept in the SLR.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal stability scheme** is a facility provided by the **RBI **to banks to borrow funds in case of temporary liquidity mismatches.
 
• **Open market operations** are the buying and selling of government securities by the **RBI** to regulate the money supply in the economy.
 
• **Legal deposit ratio** is not a commonly used term in banking.
